8 real Li-ion cells. NASA PCoE and CALCE CS2 data.

Eight batteries, from first charge to recycling

Real lithium-ion cells, aged in the lab until they failed. The AI reads their health from charging data, predicts what is left, decides each one's second life, and signs every step into a Digital Battery Passport.

  • First life, 80% and above
  • Second life, 60 to 80%
  • Recycling, below 60%

      How good are the models?

      Every number on this page is leave-one-cell-out: the model is trained on three cells and scored on the fourth, then rotated. With only four cells per dataset, this is the honest way to measure accuracy.

      State-of-health estimation

      Error by model (lower is better)

      Primary model, cell by cell

      RMSE on each unseen cell and the share of its cycles inside the 95% conformal interval.

      CellModelRMSEMAEMax errorIn 95% band

      Which signals the chosen model depends on

      Permutation importance on unseen cells: how much the error rises when one signal is shuffled.

      How to read this

      Each model is trained on three cells. On the fourth, one input column at a time is shuffled, which breaks its link to health. If the error jumps, the model was relying on that signal. If nothing changes, the model ignores it.

      Unlike the built-in importance of tree models (next row), this works for any model and is measured on data the model never saw.

      What the Gradient Boosting model relies on

      Share of impurity reduction, averaged over the four folds.

      Signals vs SOH (correlation)

      Pearson r on cleaned cycles. Positive means the signal falls as the cell ages.

      Remaining-useful-life prediction

      Error relative to the average life to 80%, so both datasets share one scale.

      Mean error as a share of life (lower is better)

      Details

      DatasetMethodMAE, cyclesAt 25% of lifeAt 50%At 75%80% band coverage

      Raw quantile bands covered only 22-33% of true values. Conformalised quantile regression widens them using errors on the training cells, bringing coverage near the 80% target.

      Second-life decisions

      When a battery leaves its first job, the system grades it from its estimated health, resistance growth and predicted remaining cycles, then picks the most demanding use it can still serve. If the uncertainty crosses a grade boundary, it asks for a lab test instead of guessing.

      Assess a battery

      Move the sliders to grade any battery with the same rules the pipeline uses.

      How often the AI grade matches the lab grade

      Grade agreement on unseen cells

      Rows are the grade a perfect lab test gives; columns are the AI's grade.

      Predicted second-life length (CALCE)

      Cycles from retirement to 60% SOH, predicted against what each cell actually did.

      Rules and assumptions

      Application requirements and value coefficients are project assumptions, set in batterylife/config.py.

      GradeUseMin SOHMax resistanceMin cycles leftCycles a year

      Value assumptions

      CO2 avoided is an upper bound: it assumes the repurposed battery fully replaces a new one of the same usable capacity. The footprint is a mid value of the 61-106 kg CO2e per kWh published by IVL for NMC production.

      Assess your own battery data

      Give the system a file with one row per charge-discharge cycle. It works out each battery's health, forecasts the cycles it has left, grades it for a second life, and issues a signed Digital Battery Passport. Put several batteries in one file to get them ranked.

      Assessing files and issuing passports is reserved for the Assessor role. You are viewing as a public visitor.

      *Capacity can be left out if all the charging signals and resistance are present and the cell type is one of the two trained types. Then health is estimated by the AI model alone, with no discharge test.

      Battery

      How to read the result

      Health

      Health is measured capacity divided by rated capacity, smoothed over nine cycles. If the file has charging signals for a trained cell type, the AI estimate is shown next to it so you can see how close the model is.

      Cycles left

      Two trend methods extend the health curve to 80% and 60%. The range between them is shown. These trend forecasts are rough: on the laboratory cells they were off by a quarter to more than the full life. Treat them as a guide.

      Confidence

      If the grade would change at the lower health bound, or between the two forecasts, the result is marked low confidence and a laboratory capacity test is recommended before the battery is redeployed.

      Digital Battery Passports

      Each battery has a passport built only from signed events. Every event carries the hash of the one before it and an Ed25519 signature from the actor who issued it, so any edit, deletion or forgery is detected. The content follows the access tiers of EU Regulation 2023/1542 (Annex XIII).

      Loading passport…

      The passport network

      Every signed passport event is an interaction between an actor and a battery. Read together, the events form a network: who hands batteries to whom, and which lifecycle steps follow which. Network measures show who the passport system depends on most.

      Who hands batteries to whom

      An arrow from A to B is drawn each time B signs the next event after A on the same battery. Thicker arrows mean more hand-offs.

      Hand-off network of actors

      Circle size shows PageRank. Hover a circle or an arrow for its numbers.

      Actor measures

      ActorBatteriesEventsInOutBetweennessPageRank

      Which step follows which

      The same events as a process map: an arrow from one event type to the next one recorded on the same battery.

      Process network of lifecycle events

      Circle size shows how often the step occurs in a transition.

      Lifecycle paths taken

      Milestones each battery passed, in order. Repeated health checks are left out.

        How to read the measures

        In and out

        Weighted degree. In counts hand-offs an actor receives; out counts hand-offs it passes on.

        Betweenness

        Share of shortest paths between other actors that pass through this one. High means it is a broker: remove it and others are cut off.

        PageRank

        Importance from incoming hand-offs, weighted by how important the senders are.

        Density and reciprocity

        Density is the share of possible links that exist. Reciprocity is the share of links that also run the other way.

        This network is small because the study has nine batteries and six registered actors. The method is the same at any scale: it is computed from the signed events with NetworkX, so new passports and actors extend it automatically.

        REST API

        Everything on this site is also available to other software through a versioned REST API. Reading is open. Changing anything needs a signed-in role, and the role decides what is allowed.

        Getting started

        Base address and sign-in

        All paths start with /api/v1. Sign in to get a token, then send it with each request in the Authorization header. Tokens last 8 hours.

        
      
        The machine-readable description is at /api/v1/openapi.json (OpenAPI 3.0). Errors always come back as {"error": {"code", "message"}}.

        Checked by the API, and again by the passport ledger when an event is signed.

        Roadmap
        The software is ready for each phase; only the hardware changes.
        
  
          
    
        1. Bench logger, one 18650 cellESP32, INA219 current sensor, DS18B20 temperature probe, TP4056 charger, MOSFET load. About INR 1,500. Firmware is in hardware/firmware.
          2. 
    
        2. Real battery management systemsRead pack voltage, current, temperature and the BMS's own SOH over CAN bus or Modbus, mapped to the same JSON protocol.
          3. 
    
        3. Fleet and passport registryMQTT from every pack to a time-series database, this pipeline as a scheduled job, and each passport's chain head anchored in the battery passport registry.

        Safety rules built into the firmware
        
      
          
        
        • Hard stop above 4.25 V, below 2.50 V, or above 55 °C: charger and load both switched off.
          • 
        
        • Charger and load are never on together; the firmware switches both off before changing state.
          • 
        
        • Fuse on the cell's positive lead; protected cells or a protection board only.
          • 
        
        • Cycle inside a fire-safe container; never charge a swollen, dented or hot cell.
